newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Jan credit rating remains stable at DB3a.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Jan credit rating remains stable at DB3a.

text.p: Slovenia's credit rating remained stable in January despite lack of progress in forming a new government and a strong tolar hurting exports, Dun and Bradstreet's (D&B) Ljubljana representative said on Wednesday.
"The general elections held on November 10 resulted in a high-degree of fragmentation in the 90-seat parliament," the agency said in its latest Risk & Payment Review.
D&B gave Slovenia, for the seventh successive month, an unchanged DB3a credit rating for January, placing it second in the region behind the Czech Republic and ahead of Poland.
The November general election gave neither right nor left a clear mandate to run the government.
Acting Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek's chances of returning to power received a boost on Wednesday when a member of the rival Christian Democrats defected, vowing to support the premier.
The support of deputy Ciril Pucko would give Drnovsek the one extra vote he needs to secure an absolute majority.
A parliamentary vote on Drnovsek's candidacy was postponed from Wednesday morning and it was not clear whether voting would go ahead later in the day.
D&B estimated real growth of 3.1 percent for 1996, down from 3.5 percent in 1995.
"This highlights the need to implement politically awkward structural reforms," the agency said.

D&B said said the government must promote industrial competitiveness through the development of small businesses, which account for only 20 percent of the total. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
